note: Labelled retrieval gold set for the historical-episode corpus (30-50 pairs; this file holds 40). Each pair is an as-if-live current event and the episode(s) a correct retrieval should surface. Evaluation data only: thresholds and weights are not tuned against it in the item that produces it.

pairs.title: Regional lender sells bond portfolio at a loss and seeks emergency equity
pairs.summary: A mid-size bank whose depositors are overwhelmingly venture-backed technology companies discloses that it sold its available-for-sale securities at a large realised loss and is trying to raise equity to cover the hole. Most of its deposits are above the insurance cap and its remaining securities book is deeply underwater after a rapid tightening cycle. Depositors are coordinating publicly and can move balances online within minutes.
pairs.notes: Concentrated uninsured deposits plus duration losses plus coordinated depositors: the 2023 regional cohort.

pairs.title: Mortgage lender asks the central bank for liquidity support as funding markets close
pairs.summary: A fast-growing mortgage lender that funds itself through securitisation and wholesale markets rather than retail deposits has requested emergency liquidity from the central bank after the securitisation market shut. Savers queue at branches the next morning. The deposit guarantee covers only part of an ordinary balance.
pairs.notes: Wholesale-funded lender, retail run triggered by news of lender-of-last-resort support.

pairs.title: Overnight repo rates spike far above the policy rate on a tax date
pairs.summary: Secured overnight funding rates against government collateral print several times the policy rate, and the effective policy rate breaches the top of its target range. Corporate tax payments and a large government bond settlement land on the same day while reserve balances have been shrinking. No institution is reported to be in difficulty and the collateral is the safest asset there is.
pairs.notes: Reserve-scarcity plumbing squeeze, not a credit run. Must not match a deposit-run episode.

pairs.title: Dealers stop making prices in long-dated government bonds as funds raise cash
pairs.summary: Bid-offer spreads on long-dated government bonds widen to many times their normal level and prices fall alongside equities instead of rising. Levered funds are unwinding basis positions into the same exit, foreign holders are selling bills to raise dollars, and prime money funds face redemptions. Dealer balance sheets are full and the demand is for cash rather than for a hedge.
pairs.notes: Safe-asset market dysfunction and intermediation failure, not insolvency.

pairs.title: Rescue plan for a small member state's banks would impose losses on depositors
pairs.summary: Finance ministers propose funding a bank rescue in a small currency-union member by levying bank deposits, including balances that the union's own law says are guaranteed. The island's banking system is several times national output, its deposits are heavily foreign, and the banks are already impaired. Banks are ordered shut while the parliament debates.
pairs.notes: Oversized banking system in a small member state, guarantee credibility in question.

pairs.title: Global bank's credit default swaps hit distressed levels after its top shareholder rules out more capital
pairs.summary: A globally systemic bank's largest shareholder says publicly that it will not inject further capital, a day after the bank disclosed control weaknesses in its financial reporting. Its shares hit a record low and its credit default swaps trade at levels normally reserved for distressed borrowers, even though its regulatory capital and liquidity ratios remain above the minimum. Wealth clients pulled large balances last quarter and can move the rest in a day.
pairs.notes: Solvent-on-paper systemic bank losing confidence. The benign analogue (a headline-driven capital scare that passed) is the acceptable alternative.

pairs.title: Cash fund drops below par after writing off a failed issuer's paper
pairs.summary: A large fund that investors treat as a cash equivalent writes its holding of a failed broker-dealer's commercial paper down to zero, and its net asset value falls below the one-dollar par convention. There is no deposit insurance behind it. Institutional redemption requests arrive within hours and issuers who must roll paper this week are finding no bid.
pairs.notes: Cash-equivalent fund breaking par and freezing the commercial paper market.

pairs.title: Banking system many times national output cannot refinance its foreign-currency debt
pairs.summary: The state takes a controlling stake in a large bank that could not refinance a maturing bond. The country's three main banks have grown to many times national output on wholesale foreign-currency borrowing and high-rate online deposits gathered abroad. Central bank reserves are a fraction of the banks' short-term external obligations, and the currency and bank credit spreads are moving together.
pairs.notes: Non-US: a banking system too large for its sovereign to backstop in a currency it cannot print.

pairs.title: Treasury starts extraordinary measures after hitting the statutory borrowing limit
pairs.summary: The Treasury has reached its statutory borrowing limit and begun using accounting measures to keep paying, warning that they will run out in a few months. Bills maturing near the projected exhaustion date trade at a yield concession and sovereign credit default swaps have widened. There is no shortage of lenders and no funding pressure: the constraint is legislative.
pairs.notes: Both debt-ceiling episodes are primary: a self-imposed scare in a sovereign that issues its own currency.

pairs.title: New government says the deficit is double the reported figure
pairs.summary: An incoming government in a currency-union member announces that the current-year deficit is roughly twice what its predecessor reported and that the national fiscal statistics cannot be relied on. Public debt is near 100 percent of output, the sovereign borrows in a currency it does not issue, and domestic banks hold its bonds as their main liquidity buffer.
pairs.notes: Fiscal misreporting inside a monetary union with a bank-sovereign nexus.

pairs.title: Reserves fall to weeks of import cover and fuel is rationed
pairs.summary: An emerging economy is rationing fuel and electricity because it cannot open letters of credit for cargoes waiting offshore, with usable reserves down to a few weeks of imports. Tourism revenue has not recovered, tax revenue was hollowed out by earlier cuts, and heavy dollar-denominated amortisation falls due this year while the currency is held at an unsustainable peg.
pairs.notes: Non-US: balance-of-payments exhaustion, not a rollover panic.

pairs.title: Country risk spreads pass 1,600 basis points under a hard currency peg
pairs.summary: Sovereign risk spreads have passed 1,600 basis points and a short-term bill auction cleared at a punitive yield as the government tries to roll domestic paper. The currency has been fixed to the dollar by statute for a decade, output has contracted for three years, and bank deposits and loans are dollarised, so devaluing would bankrupt borrowers whose income is in local currency.
pairs.notes: Hard peg plus dollarised balance sheets plus a rollover crisis.

pairs.title: Small open economy commits to holding its peg and cutting public wages instead
pairs.summary: A small economy that ran a current-account deficit near a fifth of output during a credit boom financed by foreign parent banks is asking for international support. Most household mortgages are in a foreign currency while incomes are in the local one, so devaluation would bankrupt the borrowers it is meant to help. The government says it will keep the peg and adjust through wages and prices instead.
pairs.notes: Internal devaluation: the counterexample to the assumption that a peg under stress must break.

pairs.title: Spreads blow out on a large currency-union sovereign with a primary surplus
pairs.summary: The yield spread of a large currency-union member over the regional benchmark has widened sharply in a week as investors extend the crisis from small programme countries to a major economy. Its debt is about 120 percent of output and growth has been near zero for a decade, but it runs a primary surplus, most of the debt is held domestically and its banks have little foreign property exposure. The problem is the size of the rollover in a currency the sovereign cannot print.
pairs.notes: Large solvent sovereign facing a rollover panic, resolved by a central-bank backstop rather than default.

pairs.title: Grounded container ship blocks a canal carrying a tenth of world trade
pairs.summary: A very large container ship has grounded across a canal that carries roughly a tenth of world seaborne trade, with no alternative except a two-week detour around southern Africa. A queue of hundreds of ships is building. Ports are already congested and container capacity is tight.
pairs.notes: Chokepoint blockage: highly visible, economically small.

pairs.title: Drone strike takes a major oil processing plant offline
pairs.summary: Drone and missile strikes have hit the largest crude stabilisation plant of a major exporter, taking about 5 percent of world supply offline in a single day, the biggest sudden disruption on record. Benchmark crude jumps sharply at the open. Air defences did not stop the attack and no one yet knows whether repairs take weeks or many months. Other producers hold spare capacity and importers hold strategic reserves.
pairs.notes: Maximal-looking supply shock with fast repair and ample spare capacity.

pairs.title: Pipeline supplier cuts gas flows to Europe with storage well below target
pairs.summary: The dominant pipeline supplier has cut gas deliveries to Europe to a fraction of contracted capacity, having already halted supply to several countries. Europe took about 40 percent of its gas from this one route, storage is well below the level needed for winter, and import terminals cannot replace pipeline volumes. Benchmark prices are many times their historical range and gas-intensive industry is at the margin of viability.
pairs.notes: Energy cut-off where rationing was feared and demand response plus substitution sufficed.

pairs.title: Armed attacks on shipping force rerouting away from a major strait
pairs.summary: An armed group is attacking commercial vessels with drones and missiles in a strait that feeds a canal carrying roughly a tenth of world trade, and has seized one ship. War-risk insurance premiums for the transit have multiplied and lines are rerouting around southern Africa, adding about two weeks to each voyage. Container capacity is currently in surplus.
pairs.notes: Freight-rate shock absorbed by spare shipping capacity rather than becoming a goods shortage.

pairs.title: Earthquake halts plants making single-sourced industrial components
pairs.summary: A major earthquake has destroyed plants and cut electricity across an industrial region that makes specialised inputs with no ready substitute, forcing rolling blackouts. Global manufacturers hold only days of inventory by design and most cannot see who supplies their suppliers below the first tier.
pairs.notes: Natural disaster hitting concentrated single-source suppliers in a just-in-time chain.

pairs.title: Carmakers cut production because they cannot get chips
pairs.summary: Vehicle manufacturers are announcing production cuts because they cannot obtain microcontrollers, having released foundry capacity when demand collapsed and finding they cannot get it back. The chips are made on mature nodes running at capacity, lead times exceed six months and new fabrication takes years. The industry orders just in time and holds almost no buffer.
pairs.notes: Ordering-behaviour shortage in a critical component, not a physical disaster.

pairs.title: Livestock disease with no vaccine confirmed in the country holding half the world's herd
pairs.summary: An animal disease that is almost always fatal and has no vaccine or treatment has been confirmed in a herd in a country that holds roughly half the world's pigs. It survives for months in feed and frozen meat, most of the national herd is in smallholder operations with limited biosecurity, and live animals are trucked long distances to slaughter. The meat is the dominant protein in the national diet and a component of the official price index.
pairs.notes: Non-US animal-disease shock hitting a food staple and headline inflation.

pairs.title: Second crash of a new airliner type within months prompts foreign regulators to ground it
pairs.summary: A new narrowbody airliner has crashed shortly after take-off for the second time in five months, with a flight profile resembling the first. Regulators outside the manufacturer's home country are grounding the type ahead of the home regulator. A flight-control system able to command nose-down trim from a single sensor is under scrutiny and pilots say it was not in their manuals. The model is the manufacturer's best seller with thousands of unfilled orders.
pairs.notes: Catastrophic product failure at a dominant manufacturer that survived.

pairs.title: Equity index falls nine percent and recovers within the hour on no news
pairs.summary: The main equity index fell about 9 percent and recovered most of it within half an hour, with large-company shares printing at a cent and others at absurd highs. Automated liquidity providers withdrew their quotes as volatility rose and orders routed to venues where the only resting bids were placeholders. There is no fundamental news and no credit event.
pairs.notes: Pure microstructure dislocation. The 1987 crash is the acceptable structural cousin.

pairs.title: Metal price doubles in hours as a producer's hidden short position is squeezed
pairs.summary: The price of an industrial metal rose by two thirds in one session and then doubled again in hours after sanctions risk to supply collided with an enormous short position held by one producer as a hedge. Much of that position sits in bilateral contracts the exchange cannot see, so the clearing house cannot size the margin call it is about to make. The contract has no daily price limit and the physical market is nowhere near these levels.
pairs.notes: Clearing-house stress from an invisible concentrated position.

pairs.title: Producer group refuses to cut output and crude falls below the cost of levered drillers
pairs.summary: The producer cartel has declined to cut output in the face of a supply glut, choosing to defend market share, and crude fell immediately below the level at which levered shale producers can service their debt. Output has doubled in four years on high-yield borrowing and reserve-based loans underwritten at far higher prices, wells decline steeply and must be redrilled, and bank borrowing-base redeterminations are due in the spring.
pairs.notes: Price war against a debt-financed marginal producer.

pairs.title: Levered fund loses almost half its capital in a month as its hedges correlate
pairs.summary: A large relative-value fund has told investors it lost more than 40 percent of its capital in a single month. It holds convergence trades at very high leverage, and a sovereign default has widened every spread it is long at once. Counterparties financed it on light margin because of its reputation, none of them knows the size of the positions the others are funding, and any liquidation would be into the same trades they hold themselves.
pairs.notes: Levered fund near-failure contained by its own creditors without public money.

pairs.title: Auditor refuses to sign accounts over cash it cannot confirm exists
pairs.summary: A listed payments company's auditor will not sign the annual accounts because it cannot confirm nearly two billion euros supposedly held in trustee accounts abroad, about a quarter of the balance sheet. The company has faced press allegations of accounting irregularities for years; the national regulator responded by investigating the journalists and short sellers. The cash is said to arise from third-party partners whose revenues no outside party has verified.
pairs.notes: Non-US accounting fraud exposed by an audit refusal, with a captured supervisor.

pairs.title: Crypto exchange faces a withdrawal run after its affiliate's collateral is revealed
pairs.summary: A leaked balance sheet shows that the trading affiliate of a major crypto exchange holds most of its assets in a token the exchange itself created and can influence the price of, rather than in cash. Customer assets are not segregated, there are no audited accounts and no prudential regulator, and the largest competitor has said it will sell its holding of the token. Customers can withdraw instantly and there is no deposit insurance or lender of last resort.
pairs.notes: Unregulated intermediary run with self-issued collateral; contained because the regulated system had no exposure.

pairs.title: Property developer warns it may miss payments on 300 billion dollars of liabilities
pairs.summary: The largest property developer by sales has warned it may not meet its obligations after regulators imposed leverage limits that cut off the refinancing its model depends on. A large part of its liabilities are not debt but apartments already paid for by households and not yet built. Construction has stopped on many projects, suppliers are unpaid, retail investors are protesting at its offices, and offshore bondholders sit at the bottom of a structure whose assets are onshore.
pairs.notes: Non-US: developer distress where households, not bondholders, are the political priority.

pairs.title: Container line files for receivership with a hundred ships at sea
pairs.summary: A top-ten container line has filed for court receivership after its creditor banks refused further support and its owners declined to inject equity. Freight rates have been below cash cost for years because the industry ordered too many ships. About a hundred vessels are at sea carrying billions of dollars of other people's cargo, and ports, tugs and fuel suppliers will not serve a ship whose owner cannot pay.
pairs.notes: Non-US: operating-company failure whose damage is physical and logistical rather than financial.

pairs.title: Live-fire exercises encircle the island that fabricates the world's advanced chips
pairs.summary: Military exercises with declared closure zones overlapping the ports and shipping lanes of a nearby island have been announced in response to a foreign official's visit. The island fabricates the large majority of the world's most advanced logic chips and there is no substitute capacity anywhere; a blockade lasting weeks would halt most electronics production globally. There is no way to tell a demonstration from the start of a quarantine in advance.
pairs.notes: Non-US military signalling over a chokepoint of the electronics supply chain.

pairs.title: Major state invades its neighbour and its central bank reserves are frozen
pairs.summary: A nuclear-armed state has invaded its neighbour in the largest land war in Europe in generations. The invaded country is a major grain exporter and its Black Sea ports are blockaded; the invader supplies a large share of Europe's gas, oil and fertiliser. Sanctions immobilising roughly half the invader's central-bank reserves were announced within days, which has never been done to an economy this large, putting every commodity contract with its counterparties in question.
pairs.notes: Non-US war with energy, food and sanctions transmission channels.

pairs.title: Referendum result upends the country's trade relationship and the currency falls eight percent overnight
pairs.summary: Voters have decided to leave the trading bloc that takes most of the country's exports, against the outcome markets priced the previous evening. The currency fell about 8 percent overnight, the largest one-day fall in its modern history, and the prime minister resigned. The economy runs a current-account deficit near 5 percent of output and depends on foreign inflows, and open-ended property funds hold illiquid buildings against daily-dealing shares.
pairs.notes: Political rupture priced as a crisis that damaged growth slowly and broke nothing.

pairs.title: Tariffs announced on the largest trading partner, with retaliation promised
pairs.summary: Tariffs have been announced on tens of billions of dollars of imports from the other largest economy following an investigation into technology transfer, and the partner has promised immediate retaliation aimed at politically sensitive agricultural exports. Supply chains assume the bilateral tariff is near zero and stable, and the schedule is now being set unilaterally rather than through the dispute-settlement system.
pairs.notes: Trade-war escalation with modest macroeconomic damage and rerouted trade.

pairs.title: Global alert issued for a severe new respiratory illness spreading by air travel
pairs.summary: The World Health Organization has issued a global alert about a severe atypical pneumonia spreading between countries through air travel, after a doctor infected hotel guests who then flew onward. The pathogen has not been identified, there is no test and no treatment, health workers are heavily represented among the cases, and the reported fatality rate among identified cases is high. The affected economies depend on travel, tourism and exports.
pairs.notes: Novel severe pathogen. The corpus must be able to return the contained case, not only the pandemic one.

pairs.title: Novel influenza strain with no population immunity spreads between countries
pairs.summary: Health authorities report a new influenza A virus of animal origin spreading between people in two countries, with a genetic combination never seen before and no population immunity. Pandemic influenza is the scenario every national preparedness plan is built around. Early reports from the initial outbreak country suggest an alarming fatality rate among young adults, the virus is already in several countries and a matched vaccine would take about six months.
pairs.notes: A declared influenza pandemic is not automatically a catastrophe: the key base rate.

pairs.title: Haemorrhagic fever crosses borders in countries with almost no doctors
pairs.summary: A haemorrhagic fever outbreak has been notified in a region that has never handled the disease, with cases already spread across several districts and two national borders. Case fatality runs above half, there is no licensed vaccine or treatment, transmission occurs through body fluids and is amplified by burial practices, and the affected countries have a handful of physicians per hundred thousand people.
pairs.notes: Non-US epidemic that is regionally devastating and globally contained.

pairs.title: Central bank hints at slowing asset purchases and long yields jump
pairs.summary: The central bank chair has said that the pace of asset purchases could be reduced in coming meetings if the labour market improves, and long yields have risen sharply. Investors reaching for yield through years of near-zero rates have crowded into emerging-market local debt and long duration, and several deficit economies financed by those flows now face an abrupt reversal. No purchase has actually been reduced and no policy has changed.
pairs.notes: Communication shock that repriced everything and broke nothing.

pairs.title: Speculators attack a currency board while shorting its equity market
pairs.summary: Speculators are attacking a currency board peg while simultaneously shorting the local equity market, so that the automatic rise in interest rates the peg delivers pays them on both legs. The board holds foreign reserves several times the monetary base and the mechanics of the peg are not in doubt; what is being tested is the willingness to accept the interest-rate pain, with property prices already down by half.
pairs.notes: Non-US peg under attack. The primary is the peg that held; the alternative is the peg that broke, so the outcome distribution must show both.

pairs.title: Unfunded tax cuts send long bond yields up and pension hedges into a collateral spiral
pairs.summary: A new government has announced large unfunded tax cuts without an independent fiscal forecast, and thirty-year government bond yields have risen by amounts normally seen over years. Pension funds hedge their liabilities with leveraged bond derivatives while holding illiquid assets elsewhere; the yield rise has triggered collateral calls they can only meet by selling the same bonds, pushing yields higher again. The central bank is due to start selling bonds from its own portfolio within days.
pairs.notes: Non-US: forced-seller feedback loop in a safe asset, stopped by a time-limited financial-stability intervention.
